surprises.body: St. Louis’s bottom-six forwards played 37% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 43% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

story.head: Boldy bags a hat trick
paras: Jonatan Berggren struck first for the Blues on the power play less than two minutes in. Matt Boldy and Danila Yurov scored less than four minutes apart early in the first to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. It was a busy second period. Mason McTavish made it 2-2 for St. Louis early in the period. Boldy and Kirill Kaprizov scored less than four minutes apart later in the period to put the Wild up 4-2. Boldy completed his hat trick late in the second to make it 5-2, and that one stood up as the winner. Robert Thomas cut Minnesota’s lead to 5-3 shorthanded with four minutes left. With the goalie pulled and 15 seconds left, Dylan Holloway pulled the Blues within one, but the Wild held on. Two players had three-point nights: Kaprizov with a goal and two assists, and the Blues’ Cam Fowler with three assists.

The Blues were outshot 38-25, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. The Blues hit a post and the crossbar and came up a goal short. Jesper Wallstedt made 21 saves for the Wild, and Joel Hofer allowed five goals on 38 shots. The Wild improved to 5-2-1 and climbed to second in the Central, while the Blues fell to 3-3-1, fifth in the Central.

items.text: Quinn Hughes has a point in every game this season.
Kirill Kaprizov extended his point streak against St. Louis to seven games.
The Wild won without Jared Spurgeon, Marcus Foligno, Olli Määttä and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team was missing more at the time.
Robert Thomas scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 16.
